guide.subtitle: Busan · Codex Goal Participant Guide
guide.problemStatementsIntro: The goal is to show a working result built with Codex Goal and current AI models in a half-day sprint.
guide.track1Tagline: Build an extension people can plug into Codex and use immediately.
guide.track1Desc: Create a Codex extension track submission: a Skill, MCP server, workflow, or tool package that other participants can install and try.
guide.track1Bullet1: It reduces a real repeated workflow once connected to Codex.
guide.track1Bullet2: Setup instructions, config, and README are clear enough for another builder to follow.
guide.track1Bullet3: It is more than a prompt collection: it ships as a reusable tool, skill, or workflow.
guide.track1Bullet4: The demo shows Codex calling the plugin and producing a useful result.
guide.track1Stack: Examples: K-skill, an MCP for a SaaS tool, local file/browser/terminal tools, or a workflow package a team can reuse.
guide.track1Think: Think: any domain is fine. What matters is that it plugs into Codex and becomes usable immediately.
guide.track2Tagline: Use GPT Image models as the core interface of a service.
guide.track2Desc: Build a service where image generation or editing is not a side feature, but the main product experience.
guide.track2Bullet1: Images are central to the input, output, editing loop, or app/game assets.
guide.track2Bullet2: It goes beyond a one-shot image generator and creates a repeatable user flow.
guide.track2Bullet3: Text, image, and UI connect into something people can save, share, edit, or play.
guide.track2Bullet4: The use case avoids copyright, likeness, and prohibited-content traps.
guide.track2CodexRequired: Examples: generate game assets into a mini game, character/item cards, menu/poster/thumbnail tools, or image editing workflows.
guide.track2Think: Think: not a button that makes images, but an app that exists because images can be made and edited.
guide.trackTableRow1: Scored on|Installability · Codex integration · reuse|Image experience · completeness · fun|Local grounding · field feel · conviction|Service quality · AI use · usability
guide.trackTableRow2: Required proof|Codex connection demo and README|GPT Image-based generation/editing flow|Busan/Gyeongnam material is core to the product|A working app where AI is central
guide.trackTableRow3: Why it is good|Other builders can use it immediately|The service only works because images are native|Local context makes the demo stronger|It is the most open path to a great AI app
guide.trackTableRow4: Keywords|skill, MCP, workflow, installable|image generation, editing, game asset, visual UX|port, tourism, manufacturing, market, culture|realtime, voice, agent, multimodal, service
guide.trackTableRow5: Reference|K-skill, automation MCPs, workflow packages|image asset games, card generators, poster tools|port/logistics, manufacturing SOPs, Jagalchi/Nampo, ocean content|GPT Realtime voice apps, copilots, AI games, productivity tools
guide.trackTableNote: Declare your track at submission. Prizes are awarded per track.
guide.notToDoIntro: Projects will be immediately disqualified if they fall into any of these categories:
guide.discordIntro: Join the Ralphthon Discord for team formation, announcements, and Q&A:
guide.rule1: Team Size: Maximum 4 members per team. Solo participants are welcome.
guide.rule2: Track Lock-in: One team, one track. Declare at submission.
guide.rule3: Open Source: Submitted repositories must be public.
guide.rule4: New Work Only: You may not present existing projects as your own work. Judges will check.
guide.rule5: Demo Requirements: Your demo must highlight only features built during the hackathon. Failure to clearly identify original contributions = disqualification.
guide.rule6: Codex usage encouraged: show how Codex Goal, Skills, MCP, image models, or other AI tools helped you ship faster and demo better.
guide.rule7: Banned Projects: Projects will be disqualified if they violate legal, ethical, or platform policies, or use code/data/assets you don't have rights to.
guide.mediaNoticeText: Photos or video may be taken for event documentation. If you prefer not to appear, tell the organizers at check-in.
guide.judgingDesc: Casual demos: 3 minutes per team, focused on a real working screen rather than slides.
guide.judgingNote: Clearly show what you built during the event. Working demos beat polished decks.
guide.judgingScorecardDesc: One card per judge per team.
guide.judgingScoreHeader: Team name|Judge name|Live demo (0-4)|Creativity / Originality (0-3)|Impact potential (0-3)
guide.judgingC1: Live Demo (0-4)|How well does the team implement the core idea? Does it actually work live?
guide.judgingC2: Creativity / Originality (0-3)|Has this been seen before? Does it tackle the track's problem in an original way?
guide.judgingC3: Impact Potential (0-3)|Will this survive past the hackathon? How useful is it?
guide.judgingTracks: All four tracks use the same scorecard, with judges also checking how well the submission fulfills its chosen track promise.
guide.contact: Questions? Reach out to GB Jeong — bong@team-attention.com
guide.track3Tagline: Use Busan as material, not homework.
guide.track3Desc: Instead of forcing a local problem, use Busan/Gyeongnam assets such as ports, tourism, manufacturing, the sea, markets, and local culture.
guide.track3Bullet1: The demo is more useful or more interesting because it is grounded in Busan.
guide.track3Bullet2: It uses field-like inputs such as port/logistics documents, factory photos, market/tourism routes, or local language.
guide.track3Bullet3: It picks a small situation a local user could try in a day.
guide.track3Bullet4: Local context is connected to the product function, data, or UX, not just decoration.
guide.track3Closing: Examples: multilingual port label/checklist tools, manufacturing SOP checkers, photo-based guides for Jagalchi/Nampo visitors, or games using Busan dialect and ocean imagery.
guide.track3Think: Think: not solving Busan as a problem, but using Busan as an unfair advantage.
guide.track4Tagline: An open track for any application powered by AI.
guide.track4Desc: If your build does not fit Codex Plugin, Image-native, or Busan Local Advantage, this is the open service track. Any app is welcome if AI is central to the product.
guide.track4Bullet1: Text, voice, image, realtime, agents, search, automation, and multimodal AI are all allowed.
guide.track4Bullet2: It needs a complete app flow where a user gives input and gets a useful result.
guide.track4Bullet3: It should feel like a service with a problem, UX, and output, not just a raw model demo.
guide.track4Bullet4: The strongest submissions create an experience that only became possible because of AI.
guide.track4Closing: Examples: GPT Realtime voice input/output apps, meeting or call copilots, realtime tutors, multimodal search, agentic productivity tools, AI games, or social apps.
guide.track4Think: Think: if it does not fit the other tracks, that is fine. Build a useful or fun AI-powered app.
